instructions.question: How high on the six-rung strength ladder does the Human Design report-production job described in `action` belong? The jobs produce long personal readings for paying clients: an author writes a full report from a complete packet (exact chart data, a long prompt, a template, a style guide and reference works it reads passage by passage); the same author repairs named defects or checks the published document against its source; a controller session prepares inputs, calls live chart and geocoding services with real keys, dispatches authors, runs acceptance checks, publishes and files. The rungs are ordered by what a miss costs and by how much later work rests on the job, not by length alone. Read four signals in the description: (1) what a miss costs: a slip the next check catches; a wrong or unsupported statement that a client reads and acts on; or a wrong chart fact, template structure or setup that every later section, composite and report inherits; (2) whether a gate still stands between this job and the client (deterministic mechanical checks, full-source acceptance, a read-back check, a QA pass) or this job is itself the last check; (3) whether the object is new (the first report of its type on this platform, a new template or prompt version, the first live production run) or a repeat on an accepted template and accepted inputs; (4) whether one careful pass can hold the whole object, or the risk is that any single reader misses claims spread across long reports, so that independent checkers each taking one part would do better.
instructions.tradeoff: Each rung costs more time and tokens than the one below and buys less per step. On an independent knowledge-work evaluation (blind-graded professional tasks, Elo), the lower-cost model scores 1235, 1586, 1707, 1837 and 1866 across the five single-session rungs at $0.21, $0.86, $1.54, $4.21 and $8.92 and about 1, 3, 5, 12 and 20 minutes per task; the most capable model scores 1469, 1549, 1635, 1735 and 1758 at $1.43, $2.18, $3.48, $7.22 and $9.77 and about 3, 5, 7, 13 and 17 minutes. Reading long documents barely changes with the rung: 81 to 85% on a long-context reasoning test for both models at every rung. The sixth rung multiplies the cost again by the number of agents. So the upper rungs are earned by stakes, novelty and dependence, not by length; a rung too high wastes a multiple of the cost and time, and a rung too low risks the miss the ladder exists to prevent.

criteria: low: the cheapest rung, for steps whose miss costs almost nothing and on which nothing later rests: recording a delivery date or a link, relaying a message, filing a report that has already passed its checks, running a named script, renaming files. On the knowledge-work evaluation the lower-cost model scores 1235 here against 1586 one rung up, and the most capable model 1469 against 1549, so this rung is for work that needs no judgement, not for cheap judgement.

medium: bounded work inside a written checklist or a named fix, where the next check catches a miss and little rests on this job alone: correcting a typo or a caption whose section and defect are named, with the deterministic checks re-run afterwards; filling template fields from accepted data; comparing a published document against its source with a checklist while a deterministic comparison also runs; summarising a run's results. The lower-cost model defaults here: 1586 at $0.86 and about 3 minutes per task. Checklist reviews are weak on their own: in one study a review in the authoring session scored F1 22% and a fresh-session review 29% on planted errors, and omissions were caught only 14 to 21% of the time, so a deterministic check, not this rung, is the real gate for such work.

high: real judgement with moderate stakes, where a later gate still stands between this job and the client: a repair pass that fixes defects named at acceptance, each with its section, failed requirement and evidence; reviewing such a repair; drafting a short focused component for a returning client on an accepted template; diagnosing why a check failed. The most capable model defaults here (1635 at $3.48 per task); the lower-cost model reaches 1707 at $1.54. Repair against named defects is the case where self-correction works, because the defects arrive with their locations: given the location, models fixed 18 to 44 points more of the wrong answers. Practitioner tests of both models recommend drafting long prose at this rung or above.

extra high: long, complex, client-facing judgement where a miss reaches the client or misleads later work, with acceptance and QA still after it: writing a full 40-page reading or a two-person composite of a type already produced here, on the accepted template, from a complete packet; a routine production controller run over several reports lasting more than half an hour. Cost roughly doubles over high: the lower-cost model scores 1837 at $4.21 and about 12 minutes per task (130 Elo over high), the most capable 1735 at $7.22 (100 over high); on an independent office-deliverables evaluation (memos, decks, spreadsheets) the lower-cost model rises from 1689 at high to 1768 here.

max: the deepest single-session reasoning, for work where a miss is expensive or everything after it inherits the result: the first report of a new type, template or prompt version on this platform for a real client, whose structure later reports copy; the first live production run with real chart and geocoding calls; interpretation that must reconcile conflicting sources where no later check can judge the result; root-cause analysis after a repair has already failed. It buys little on average: the lower-cost model gains 29 Elo over extra high at 2.1 times the cost and 1.7 times the time per task, the most capable model 23 Elo at 1.35 times the cost; on a closed-book knowledge test the share of unknown answers the lower-cost model gets wrong instead of declining falls from 66% to 59% at this rung, while the most capable model's rises from 71% to 73%; in a review benchmark this rung caught 10 of 13 hard defects against 8, while precision fell from 67% to 52%. Reserve it for first-of-a-kind or irreversible work.

ultracode: the top rung, a strength level above max: many independent agents, each checking one part of the work, for work where one reader missing something is the main risk and the result must hold for everything that follows: checking every claim of the first production reports on this platform against their chart data and cited reference passages, section by section, before clients receive them; an independent review by a second model of a first-of-type report; an audit of a batch already delivered after a class of defect was found in it. Claim-by-claim checking is cheap and close to human agreement (72% agreement with human raters on about 16,000 facts, at about $0.19 per response); one fresh review by the same model plus one by a different model caught 57% of planted errors against 43% for two reviews by the same model. Gains plateau at a few independent reviewers, and multi-agent setups used 15 to 80 times the tokens of one agent, so this rung is for independence a single reader cannot supply, not for routine reports or listed repairs.

instructions.question: Which model should run the Human Design report-production job described in `action`, at whatever rung it needs?
instructions.tradeoff: Four models share the same six rungs. List prices per million input and output tokens: the most capable model $10 and $50; the strong model $4 and $20; the balanced model $2 and $10; the small fast model $0.10 and $0.50 for prompts up to 100,000 tokens ($0.50 and $2.50 above). Output speed at max: small fast 237, balanced 141, strong 97 and most capable 71 tokens per second. On an independent knowledge-work evaluation (blind-graded professional tasks, Elo) by rung, low to max: small fast 1123, 1275, 1418, 1513, 1618 at $0.01 to $0.22 per task; balanced 1175, 1323, 1549, 1728, 1838 at $0.21 to $6.84; strong 1235, 1584, 1704, 1831, 1866, $8.92 at max; most capable 1469, 1545, 1635, 1732, 1754, $9.77 at max. Office deliverables at max: balanced 1817, strong 1803, most capable 1672, small fast 1577; at medium: strong 1625, most capable 1528, balanced 1441, small fast 1372. Reading long documents: 85% for the most capable and strong models and 83% for the balanced and small fast models at max. On a closed-book knowledge test at max, the share of unknown answers given wrongly instead of declined: small fast 40%, balanced 47%, strong 59%, most capable 73%. Legal deliverables from case files with every criterion met and no material hallucination, at max: most capable 6.4%, strong 4.2%, balanced 2.8%, small fast 0.6%; material hallucinations per deliverable: strong 0.59, balanced 1.03, most capable 1.32, small fast 1.61. Legal research: most capable 55.3%, strong 50.5%, balanced 48.1%, small fast 43.3%; tax work 49.2%, 45.6%, 42.0%, 31.9%. In one practitioner test of drafting a 1,000- to 1,300-word article from a supplied brief, three drafts each at their default levels, 2 of 3 drafts by the balanced model added claims the brief did not supply, against 0 of 3 by the strong model. Between the two larger models, writing quality is close: the most capable model leads a judged creative-writing test (2162 against 2050) and a long-form test (85.3 against 84.6, neither degrading over eight chapters), while the strong model leads crowd votes on creative writing, long queries and instruction following (1516 against 1482, 1526 against 1510, 1517 against 1498); the most capable model leads on single-pass expert writing from supplied source documents (73.8 against 65.8). Reviewers found the most capable model stayed faithful to source material but overran explicit length limits, and the strong model, as an editor, sometimes produced a revision that ignored its own diagnosis. The vendor describes the small fast model as built for classification, routing, extraction and subagent tasks, and the balanced model as strongest at well-scoped everyday tasks and documents.

most_capable_model.what: Work where the depth of one pass of expert synthesis from source material decides the outcome and later work builds on it: the first report of a new type, template or prompt version on this platform; a two-person composite whose relationship mechanics must be reconciled across both charts when that report type has not been produced here before; interpretation that weighs conflicting statements across several reference works where no later check can judge it; a client's open questions whose framing is not given; or work on which the strong model at a higher rung has already fallen short.
most_capable_model.not_for: Work on an accepted template and accepted inputs with acceptance and QA behind it, or work with a written checklist or named defects: standard readings and composites of a type already produced here, repairs of named defects, checks of a published document against its source, controller steps that run written scripts, recording and filing. There 2.5 times the strong model's price and slower turns buy little, and on independent knowledge-work evaluations the strong model at extra high already outscores this one at max.
examples: Write the first parent-child composite report produced on this platform, for a paying client, from a complete packet
Reconcile two reference works that disagree about a gate's meaning before a report section is written
Rewrite a report section after two repairs by the strong model failed acceptance

strong_model.what: Long client-facing report work on an accepted template, with acceptance and QA behind it: drafting a standard single-person reading, or a composite of a type already produced here, from a complete packet; repairing defects named at acceptance and reviewing such a repair; a production controller run with live chart and geocoding calls. It leads the four on blind-graded professional tasks at max (1866) and has the fewest material hallucinations per legal deliverable (0.59 against 1.03 to 1.61), and in one brief-following test it added no unsupplied claims where the balanced model did in 2 of 3 drafts.
strong_model.not_for: The first report of a new type or template whose structure later reports copy, open-ended interpretation where no later check can catch an error, or work on which this model at a higher rung has already fallen short; and short checked steps, records, summaries and comparisons that the balanced or small fast model completes at a half or a fortieth of the price per token.
examples: Write a standard single-person reading for a returning client on the accepted template
Fix four acceptance defects that each name a section and the failed requirement
Run the controller for a routine request of three reports on accepted templates

balanced_model.what: Bounded document work with a checklist or a deterministic check behind it, where a miss is caught before a client reads it: comparing a published document against its source with a written checklist, summarising a run's results for the run log, filling template fields from accepted data, drafting run notes or a short internal summary. It is level with the strong model on office deliverables (1817 against 1803 at max) and close on reading long documents (83% against 85%), at half the price per token and about 1.5 times the output speed.
balanced_model.not_for: Writing a full client reading or composite whose statements a client reads and acts on, a first report of any type, interpretation from conflicting sources, or repairs whose evidence must be weighed: in a brief-following test 2 of 3 of its drafts added claims the brief did not supply, against none for the strong model.
examples: List every difference between a published Google Doc and its accepted Markdown source, using the formatting checklist
Write the run log entry for a completed production run from its acceptance and QA records
Fill the report header fields from the accepted client intake record

small_fast_model.what: Mechanical, high-volume or extraction steps on which nothing later rests: recording a delivery date or a link, filing, renaming files, relaying a message, running a named script, copying fields from chart data into a table that a deterministic check then compares, sorting or routing requests into given categories. The vendor builds it for classification, routing, extraction and subagent tasks, at a twentieth of the balanced model's price per token and about 1.7 times its output speed.
small_fast_model.not_for: Writing, repairing or reviewing any client-facing text, interpretation, checking a report's claims, or any controller step with live calls: on blind-graded professional tasks it scores 1618 at max against 1838 to 1866 for the balanced and strong models, and its legal deliverables averaged 1.61 material hallucinations each against 0.59 for the strong model.
examples: File an accepted report's Google Doc link on the client's Notion page
Sort this week's intake requests into the four report types the intake form defines
Rename a run's output files to the naming convention in the run plan
